The main reference is the SQLAlchemy error-messages page, which covers MissingGreenlet directly. Here's what the search turned up.

**What the error means:** The SQLAlchemy docs describe MissingGreenlet as a case where the async driver gets called from outside the greenlet context that SQLAlchemy's asyncio layer normally sets up. The exception is raised by the async greenlet await_ when it is called outside the greenlet spawn context. The usual cause is an attempt to do I/O from code that isn't awaited.

**Why it happens with the ORM:** When using the ORM this is nearly always due to the use of lazy loading, which is not directly supported under asyncio without additional steps and/or alternate loader patterns. Accessing an unloaded relationship or an expired attribute on an `AsyncSession` is the typical trigger.

**Recommended reading:**
- **"Preventing Implicit IO when Using AsyncSession"** in the asyncio extension docs. The error page points to this section as the main guide. It is at https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/21/orm/extensions/asyncio.html. The 2.0 docs have the same section.
- **Fixes described in that section:**
  - Eager loading up front is the preferred approach. The docs note that it's of course preferable to use eager loading up front in order to have collections already set up without the need to lazy-load.
  - Explicit refresh: a lazy-loaded relationship can be loaded explicitly under asyncio using AsyncSession.refresh(), if the desired attribute name is passed explicitly to Session.refresh.attribute_names.
  - Write-only relationships: collections can be replaced with write only collections that will never emit IO implicitly, by using the Write Only Relationships feature.
  - `run_sync()`: AsyncSession.run_sync() runs a Python function inside a greenlet, so synchronous-style lazy loading translates to await when it reaches the database driver.

**Version notes:**
- The 2.1 docs changed installation. The asyncio "greenlet" dependency no longer installs by default, so you need `pip install sqlalchemy[asyncio]` if you don't already have greenlet.
- The 1.4 docs describe the same error and point to the same guide, so the advice carries across versions.

I didn't find a GitHub issue tied specifically to SQLAlchemy 2.0.43. The results cover the general MissingGreenlet problem with async lazy loading, which is likely what you're hitting.

**What the error means:** The error appears when code touches a relationship that wasn't loaded in the original query. It happens when you access a Relationship attribute (like user.posts) that was not loaded in the original query. Sync SQLAlchemy would quietly run that lazy query, but under asyncio the query can't run from a plain attribute access.

**The usual fixes:** Load the relationship up front rather than lazily. One source says you must tell SQLAlchemy to fetch the related data upfront using "Eager Loading" strategies like selectinload or joinedload. Another suggests globally setting a relationship to always load its mapping by setting lazy='selectin' on the foreign relationship itself, or specifying explicit join or select conditions per query.

**Related GitHub discussion:** A sqlmodel issue (fastapi/sqlmodel #74) shows the same error with a traceback from a sync-style attribute access inside an async function. The error text there points to an older SQLAlchemy docs version (the link uses /e/14/), so it may predate 2.0.43. Check the issue thread before relying on it for version-specific behavior.

**Caveat on your version:** I couldn't confirm any 2.0.43-specific change or regression. To check for one, search the sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy GitHub issues tab for "MissingGreenlet" and filter by the 2.0.43 milestone or label, or review the 2.0.43 changelog in the SQLAlchemy docs. If you share your traceback and model setup, I can help narrow down which relationship is triggering the lazy load.


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.

The section is **"Preventing Implicit IO when Using AsyncSession"** on the Asynchronous I/O (asyncio) page. This page documents **SQLAlchemy 2.0.54**, labeled a "legacy version."

**Lazy loading**
- The guidance says that under asyncio, special care is needed to avoid "lazy loading" and expired-attribute access on relationships and columns.
- Accessing an unloaded collection normally emits database IO, which fails under asyncio because implicit IO isn't allowed.
- Relationships can be declared with `lazy="raise"` so they don't attempt to emit SQL by default. The page says collections are then loaded through eager loading.

**Eager loading**
- The page calls `selectinload()` "the most useful eager loading strategy" and uses it in the examples.
- It doesn't discuss `joinedload()` or `raiseload()` in this section. The only related option it mentions is the `lazy="raise"` setting.

**AsyncSession.refresh() with attribute_names**
- A lazy-loaded relationship can be loaded explicitly with `AsyncSession.refresh()`, but only if the attribute is named in `attribute_names`.
- Eager loading is still preferred.

**run_sync**
- `AsyncSession.run_sync()` is an optional method that runs a Python function inside a greenlet, so traditional synchronous ORM code can run within an awaitable.
- The page includes a "Deep Alchemy" caution that this goes against asyncio's usual rule of marking every IO point with `await`.

**Write-only relationships**
- Write-only collections "will never emit IO implicitly," so they are read only through explicit SQL queries.
- The page says this technique "is fully compatible with asyncio and should be preferred."
- The trade-off is that there's no built-in way to load many of these collections at once.

I could not find the Stack Overflow discussion. The search tool's user agent is blocked from stackoverflow.com, and I did not try to reach it another way. The official SQLAlchemy docs cover the same error and its fixes, so the applicability assessment below rests on those.

**The error:** `project.md` names `MissingGreenlet`, raised when an unloaded relationship is read outside the awaited query. No traceback was supplied, so the exact failing line is unknown.

**Does the advice apply to SQLAlchemy 2.0.43 with asyncpg 0.30.0?** Mostly yes, with one gap in version matching.

- The [official asyncio guide](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html), "Preventing Implicit IO when Using AsyncSession", recommends:
  - Eager loading up front, with `selectinload()` as the example strategy.
  - `lazy="raise"` on relationships, so unloaded access fails loudly instead of trying I/O.
  - `AsyncSession.refresh()` with the relationship named in `attribute_names`.
  - Write-only relationships, which never emit I/O implicitly.
  - `run_sync()`, which runs sync-style code inside a greenlet. The guide calls it a deep-alchemy option that goes against asyncio's usual rule.
- The guide documents 2.0.54, not the pinned 2.0.43. I did not check the 2.0.43 changelog, so I cannot confirm this section is identical in the pinned release. The fixed-up behavior is unlikely to differ within the 2.0 line, but that remains unverified.
- A blog snippet suggested setting `lazy='selectin'` globally on the relationship. That is a lead, not authoritative guidance. It changes loading for every query on that relationship, so treat it as a tradeoff to evaluate, not a default fix.
- A [sqlmodel issue #74](https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/issues/74) shows the same error. I saw only the search snippet and did not read the thread, so I have no confirmed version or resolution for it.
- `requirements.txt` does not list `greenlet`. The asyncio layer depends on it, so confirm it is installed in the target environment. I did not verify how this pin pulls it in.

**Recommendation for next steps (not implemented):**
1. Get the full traceback from a failing request and identify which relationship is accessed outside the awaited query.
2. Reproduce with a minimal async script on the pinned versions, `SQLAlchemy==2.0.43` and `asyncpg==0.30.0`.
3. Apply eager loading (`selectinload`) at the query that loads that object, then verify with a test that reads the relationship after the session returns.
4. Consider `lazy="raise"` on the relationship so future implicit loads fail in tests rather than in production.

**Sources:**
- [SQLAlchemy 2.0 asyncio docs](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html), read directly. It documents 2.0.54, not 2.0.43.
- [SQLAlchemy 2.0 error messages](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/errors.html), from search results.
- [fastapi/sqlmodel #74](https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/issues/74), from search snippet only.
